keep_playing_why: In A I knew what to do in 20 seconds (tap a circle, build a sandwich weapon), got a coin and pop for every olive, and every wave let me upgrade something, so the next minute always felt better. In B my own timing mistakes decided most matches and the storm, ram and gold-ring rules piled up by rival three. A's Jar boss with the SWAT prompt was a real payoff, B's Brisa just felt unfair to me.
better_made_why: A is clearer: menus, prices, stars, orders, a boss with a prompt telling me what to tap, constant coin and pop feedback and rotating music. B is very cinematic (water, camera, hit stops, rival banter, spoils cards) and arguably prettier in motion, but its three timing cues (gap mark, gold ring, storm cell) are hard to read together on a phone, the mark seemed to lag, and the 'out of reach' and 'late couch' results did not teach me what to fix.
furthest_A: Level 1 Cutting Board cleared with 3 stars (score 10,200); level 2 The Stovetop lost twice at wave 7 and wave 9/10, then beat on the 4th try incl. The Jar boss at wave 10 for 1 star (score 18,690, 3 bites left); The Sink unlocked but not played.
furthest_B: Beat three rivals in order: Pip Tiller (second match, score 2,450), Bosun Barnacle (third try, score 1,950) and Doc Volta (first try, score 2,550). Lost to the fourth rival, Contessa Brisa, about 8 times; best was within one hit (Double dunk almost x3, score 1,350). Never reached The Dock or other menu modes.
